newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: KERNOT SAYS PM SHOULD PROVE NEED FOR CHANGE TO MEDIA LAWS
Democrats leader, Cheryl Kernot, says the Prime Minister should prove the case for changing media ownership laws, before going ahead and doing it.
The Government is due to decide soon whether to scrap the cross-media ownership rules.
Seven Television Network Chairman Kerry Stokes has accused John Howard of doing deals to deliver the Fairfax Newspaper group to Kerry Packer, an accusation Mr Howard denies.
Cheryl Kernot says a decision on whether the Democrats will proceed with a Senate inquiry into media ownership rules, will be made soon.
Senator Kernot says the Prime Minister has given no justification for a change to the present rules, and it shouldn't be mogul-specific.
STRONG WIK RESPONSE WOULD COUNTER HANSON SUPPORT-RUSSELL
The National Party's Queensland President says a strong and principled response to the Wik issue would counter Pauline Hanson's argument that nobody cares about the ordinary people.
David Russell told the Young Nationals' annual State conference on the Gold Coast, both sides of politics could suffer electorally, if they don't respond effectively to the Hanson phenomenon.
He says a recent opinion poll highlighted the controversial independent's potential to translate her popularity into votes.
BHP WORKERS TO STRIKE
The ACTU has launched a campaign to reverse the planned closure of BHP's Newcastle steelworks, starting with a 24 hour nationwide strike by steel industry workers on Thursday-week.
Steel unions say BHP needs to consider it's role in the Australian manufacturing industry, and the two and a half thousand workers who'll lose their jobs, not just economic and money market issues.
ACTU President Jenny George says the government also has to involve itself in the issue, not stand by and let major industry do as it pleases.
The ACTU is not ruling out the involvement of other BHP divisions in the campaign.
NATIVE TITLE DELAY SLOWS RESOURCE EXPLORATION - REPORT
A leading economist says the delay in achieving a workable system to native title is slowing mineral exploration and development.

Dr Don Stammers, in a report for the Chamber of Minerals and Energy of Western Australia, says uncertainties over native title and land access are already having significant impact on the exploration industry.
He says it's taking longer to gain an exploration licence, and starting a mining project is much more complicated today than in the past.
Dr Stammers says maintaining Australia's high level of exploration is important, especially in the face of increasing competition for the exploration dollar in other countries.
PM'S CHIEF OF STAFF TAKING UP SOCOG JOB
The Prime Minister, John Howard, has announced his chief of Staff, Nicole Feely, is leaving his office to take up a job with the Sydney Olympic Organising Committee.
He's paid tribute to Ms Feely, saying she's played a key role in supervising the Coalition's transition to Government.
Mr Howard says she also played an important role in the process of policy co-ordination and development while the Coalition was in Opposition.
The Prime Minister has wished Ms Feely every success in her new role, which includes building links with the Government in the lead up to the Sydney 2000 Games.
JUSTICE SAYS GAMBLING PLAYING BIGGER ROLE IN DIVORCES
The Family Court Chief Justice, Alastair Nicholson, says the role of gambling in family problems is now taking on a new dimension.
Chief Justice Nicholson says an increasing number of couples involved in divorce proceedings are citing gambling as a major concern.
He says there's been a big change in gambling, with the growth of casinos, and the promotion of the TAB on a big scale.
